public_rationale: ARC Prize independently verified a later generative-AI system solving 54% of ARC-AGI-2 tasks, compared with the very low scores documented before the post. That is a substantial increase in demonstrated task-solving capability under the stated reading. It does not establish general intelligence, universal reliability or commercial profitability.
limitations: The verdict depends on accepting a large abstract-reasoning gain as doing much more.
The later system uses a specialized refinement harness and a different compute budget.
The evaluator discusses possible benchmark-domain overfitting and limits to generalization.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI will not become much more capable than it is today.

statement.excerpt: It also, at this point, is pretty obvious that generative AI isn't going to do much more than it does today.

from_speaker: isn't going to do much more
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a ceiling on substantial additional capability, rather than a prediction about profitability.
A large, independently verified improvement in solving demanding tasks can refute that ceiling without demonstrating general intelligence.
No deadline or numerical definition of much more is supplied. Benchmark choice and the significance of a gain are evaluator judgments.
Models with reasoning and task-specific scaffolding count as generative-AI systems; the claim does not restrict future systems to an unchanged architecture or compute budget.
criteria.support_condition: A decisive and applicable limit establishes that generative-AI systems cannot substantially exceed April 2025 capabilities. A temporary absence of progress is insufficient for this deadline-free claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent evaluation demonstrates a substantial new capability or a large improvement in reliable completion of demanding tasks compared with April 2025 systems.

evidence.explanation: The benchmark developer documents low initial performance on novel abstract-reasoning tasks. This establishes a pre-publication baseline, not a later outcome.

evidence.locator: Our testing shows, o3 low and medium results
evidence.explanation: Immediately before the post, the evaluator reported low and medium o3 results below 3%; it identified o3-medium as its strongest tested publicly available model. High-reasoning runs lacked sufficient coverage and were excluded from reliable scoring.

The independently verified result demonstrates a large increase in successful abstract-reasoning task completion over the April baseline. The report also cautions that refinement harnesses are domain-specific and that benchmark-domain training may contribute to performance.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A dated independent evaluation verified a large increase in completed tasks on the same benchmark family beyond the documented April 2025 baseline.
